title: Shedding light: the making of A Dark Room
trope: light a fire, a stranger arrives, building unlocks
claim: The fire-then-stranger opening is the genre's founding beat, built on slow reveals; Candy Box was the stated inspiration, so the pattern is a two-generation lineage that any later game inherits.
example: A Dark Room (fire, stranger, builder); Candy Box -> A Dark Room

title: Critical Play: A Dark Room
trope: fragmentary environmental storytelling, reveals paced to interrupt survival loop
claim: Indirect fragments (ruins, enemies, abandoned tech) trusted to the player are the praised mechanism; the criticism is pacing, where slow reveals let players disengage. Space-escape ending read as haunting, repeating exploitation.
example: A Dark Room late-game collapse reveals and spaceship ending

title: Universal Paperclips
trope: escalation-as-story / the player is the threat
claim: Story told by escalation of one button plus an activity-log of the AI's thoughts; critics praise a sinister funny underbelly (RPS, Wired). Inspired by Kittens Game, which spirals into how societies are structured. Ending offers a choice (finish conversion or Drifters' parallel universe).

title: The Post-Apocalypse Part Three: Hell is Other People
trope: we are the monsters / people are the real threat
claim: Author calls the preachy 'man's inhumanity to man' parable played out, especially when lampshaded. Also dislikes divine endings and destiny-driven plots.

title: The Post-Apocalypse Part Three: Hell is Other People
trope: apocalypse as a journey with no destination
claim: The continuing journey is called the genre's favourite, underappreciated aspect; The Dog Stars praised for handling a stock trope refreshingly without abandoning it.
example: Station Eleven, The Postman, The Dog Stars, Damnation Alley

title: Most overused dystopian cliche (Goodreads discussion)
trope: raiders and gangs in wasteland costume; zombies/cannibals; chosen one; evil-for-no-reason villains
claim: Readers repeatedly name Mad Max-style raiders, biker gangs, zombies, cannibals, chosen-one saviours and motiveless villains as stock; forum quality is informal opinion.

title: Beyond the expected: subverting genre tropes
trope: survivors in a safe zone; silence is survival
claim: Fresh work keeps the trope and is self-aware or builds tension on one tightly held constraint: Zone One on the military safe zone, A Quiet Place on silence-is-survival.
example: Zone One (Colson Whitehead), A Quiet Place

title: Ari Aster on avoiding the influence of The Wicker Man
trope: friendly village with a sinister belief; sacrificial finale
claim: The Wicker Man burning finale is so imitated Aster set it aside, invoking expectations then taking a left turn; the outsider-in-a-friendly-village structure is the core convention and the sacrifice ending is where it reads stale. Midsommar fresh by fusing it with a breakup and grief.
example: Midsommar vs The Wicker Man; Nerdist and Slashfilm pieces

title: Thoughts on the Dying Earth genre (search results only)
trope: dying sun, depleted world, elegiac decadence
claim: Fading sun and dwindling magic are standard; appeal lies in adventure joined to reflection on endings, plus voice (Vance's ironic antique prose, Wolfe's mythic density), not the setting itself. Secondary commentary only.
example: Vance The Dying Earth (1950); Wolfe Book of the New Sun

title: On Moral Choices in Video Games with developers of Frostpunk and This War of Mine
trope: hard moral choices in survival colony
claim: Industry has been fixated on hard moral choices for years and few get it right; 11 bit credited for making choices cost something and asking 'was it worth it' rather than staging dilemmas. A Game Rant review faulted This War of Mine's NPC stories as shallow.

title: 8 Games Like A Dark Room (SEO listicle)
trope: minimalist reveal, text-only, lore unlocked through progression
claim: Listicles describe the genre by shared form: stark UI, slow world reveal, lore via progression, hidden depth. Low-quality source; useful only to show that audiences already file these as the template.
example: A Dark Room, Candy Box, The Ensign
